text:
Matvei Gridin is a 20-year-old in his first full NHL season, and he has 10 points in 17 games, half on the power play. Flames Nation is asking what he can do over 82 games, and The Win Column wondered whether he'd go top ten in a 2024 redraft (he went 28th). That's the buzz. Here is our read.

His last ten games bring 8 points, 5 goals, against a usual pace of about 6.4. The chances behind it are normal (1.9 expected goals on his own shots over that stretch, against 2.1 usual), so we read most of it as bounces. What is real is the ice time, up more than two minutes a night lately, and how he plays. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small 8-game sample, had him carrying the puck in 61 percent of the time and getting to the home-plate area at an 86th-percentile rate.

Players taken in his range score a median 0.35 points a game in their first real season. He is at 0.59. Expect it to cool, then watch whether the minutes stick.
headline: Gridin's hot run comes with an asterisk
